page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.48xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores running on AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 silicon at 2.7 GHz, operating without hyperthreading. Cache distribution includes 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core alongside 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity reaches 1536.0 GB, providing an exact 8.0 GB allocation per core. The server includes no integrated local storage disks and does not contain discrete hardware GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage while provisioning a baseline network throughput of 400 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute and memory scalability across parallel configurations. In stress-ng, multi-core CPU execution reaches top-tier standing at 314,834.98 points, contrasting with average single-core performance of 1,643.79 points. Memory throughput benchmarks register top-tier performance, recording 21,337.88 GB/sec in cached small-block reads, 960.8 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads, and 483.48 GB/sec in uncached writes. Database handling capabilities are evidenced by 359.67 million Redis SET operations per second and high multi-threaded decompression rates in bzip3 at 1,412.6 GB/sec. Clang software compilation and CPU physics testing similarly occupy top-decile percentiles.

Hardware tradeoffs focus primarily on single-threaded constraints and the total absence of onboard NVMe storage. Single-threaded metrics, including standard Geekbench and compression runs, fall within average percentiles, while image processing scores place in the bottom 25%. Additionally, large-scale matrix and vector operations lack x86-specific extensions like AVX-512 and AMX, and prompt processing for compact 135M language models reflects lower efficiency compared to accelerated platforms. Cost efficiency emerges through high core density and broad memory allocation per physical CPU, reducing the overhead of running expansive in-memory environments.

The r8gb.48xlarge profile fits high-throughput distributed memory caches, large relational databases, in-memory analytics platforms, and enterprise build clusters requiring large memory footprints and substantial multi-threaded parallelism.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gb.48xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based server featuring 192 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V2 architecture at 2.7 GHz without multithreading. It provides 1536.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8.0 GB per core ratio, backed by 400 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth. The hardware includes no local disks and operates without GPU accelerators. Parallel performance is extensive, highlighted by top-tier results in multi-core stress testing, memory bandwidth reaching 960.8 GB/sec on uncached reads, and 359.67 million Redis operations per second. In contrast, single-thread execution and image processing register at average to below-average levels. Hardware density provides qualitative operational cost efficiency for distributed platforms that require large memory footprints and vast core concurrency. The instance is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large Redis deployments, distributed data processing, and large-scale parallel software compilation workloads.
